description: Provider-substitution dispatch-overhead experiment: identical trivial stub task, identical ShieldGovernance config, through three paths (native K9-AIF, K9CrewAIAdapter wrapping a DummyCrew, K9LangGraphAdapter wrapping a single-node compiled graph), 100 runs each, 3 independent repetitions.

comparison_to_manuscript.note: Absolute ms values differ from the manuscript by real machine variance (sub-millisecond timing is highly environment-sensitive); the CrewAI overhead range is narrower and consistently positive this run (4.7-6.2%, vs. the manuscript's -0.3% to +8.3%). The LangGraph overhead range this run is wider on the high end (up to 189.1%, driven by one repetition's higher-variance run with a max outlier of 8.346ms, likely OS scheduling noise) vs. the manuscript's 122-141%. The qualitative conclusion is unchanged and, if anything, reinforced: CrewAI overhead is negligible and within noise; LangGraph shows real, reproducible overhead from its own graph-traversal machinery, negligible next to any real LLM call. Per the 'fresh value wins' rule, this run's figures replace the manuscript's.
